source.title: A Shared Valence Axis Across Modern LLMs and Human EEG: The Saturation Regularity
source.authors: Yousef A. Radwan; Xuhui Liu; Kilichbek Haydarov; Yuqian Fu; Mohamed Elhoseiny

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or document mismatch; the supplied text includes the paper and supplementary material.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures similarity of extracted V-axis directions across models and whether EEG classifiers encode that axis, using its own PCA, cosine, and correlation analyses rather than the original studies’ methods.
record.gate_note: The paper reports direct measurements relevant to cross-model and cross-checkpoint alignment, including model-pair V-axis similarity, scale relationships, and EEG-checkpoint encoding of the V-axis. Results about auxiliary-loss effects on EEG accuracy, ensemble performance, and V-axis ablation are not included as rows: they test training or causal utility, not whether independently trained representations converge.
record.test_reason: The study's own measurements bear on cross-model agreement in a new, narrow setting: one PCA-derived valence direction compared across 14 LLMs, and EEG classifiers' alignment with that LLM direction versus their accuracy. Convergence is not the paper's main question. Its load-bearing claim is the saturation regularity, and the authors frame the probe results as direction-existence claims. Only one concept direction is compared, never full representations.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but the emphasis needs correcting. The authors' load-bearing claim is the saturation regularity: 25 V-axis supervision recipes never help, and 16 significantly hurt, once the classifier already encodes the axis. They also report a residual-diversity ensemble reaching FACED-9 state of the art. They present the shared V-axis across 14 LLMs, EEG and EEG classifiers as a probe and direction-existence claim. Within it, convergence depends on family and generation rather than size, and the class-mean classifier alignment is only trending against a random null.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses PCA on emotion-class centroids, V-axis cosine comparisons, and correlations with behavioural or EEG references rather than the original studies’ general representational-similarity and scaling approach.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported alignment varies by model family and tier, by model size relationship, by stimulus subset, and by estimator (linear correlation versus mutual information). The paper also reports layer dependence for some models, including a Gemma-4 exception to the penultimate-layer peak.

fits_no_version.finding: Alignment of the LLM V-axis with human behavioural valence and with cohort EEG, and its (absent) relation to model size: flat within Qwen3 (p = 0.24) and within the top tier (p = 0.684), plus tiers by behavioural r.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model-to-human alignment of a concept direction (behavioural ratings, EEG) tracks model family and generation rather than parameter count.

record.code_released: No code or checkpoints released with the submission; release upon acceptance is promised. No URL stated.
record.problems: The scale analysis is not a controlled scaling sweep and the authors report no size-monotonic association within Qwen3. The 36-checkpoint V-axis-specific random-direction null is only at the 93.5th percentile (one-sided p = 0.066). Cross-family comparisons use one extracted concept direction, and the study itself reports that its cohort signal depends strongly on a small stimulus subset. The paper distinguishes its full-feature ridge correlations from separate single-electrode analyses.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant result rows omitted. Training-loss accuracy changes, ensemble results, and feature ablations were excluded because they do not measure representational convergence as defined by the versions.

untested.parts: No size or capability trend in pairwise inter-LLM similarity is reported. No general representational similarity is measured, only one 1-D concept direction. Architecture, objective and data are not varied in a controlled way.
Untested. The CLIP-image V-axis is scored against OASIS valence ratings; no paired image-caption alignment across model quality is measured.
No direct seed-to-seed comparison of features or subspaces. The claim that the residual is seed-specific is inferred from ensemble gains, not measured.
Untested. Procrustes is applied to one extracted direction (R4), not used to map full representations.
Untested. No neurons, SAE features or circuits are compared across models.
No test separates shared data or objectives from a common model of reality as the cause. The authors only remark that family membership matters more than scale.

missing.what: SEED-V cross-checkpoint result on 15 CBraMod checkpoints. Accuracy vs best-PC V-axis alignment is r = 0.601 (p = 0.018). The class-PC1 estimator gives only r = 0.358 (p = 0.19).
Class-PC1 V-axis alignment by depth: d ∈ {4,6,8,10} gives 0.43, 0.43, 0.39, 0.38. This decreases with depth and seems inconsistent with the 0.60–0.77 reported for the d=6 pool.
Per-architecture class-PC1 alignment: CBraMod mean 0.21, EMOD d6 0.67, EMOD d6 e150 0.69. The gap between architectures dominates the spread within each.
Layer dependence: Gemma-4's text V-axis peaks at layer 1, not the penultimate layer. Input-layer vs final-layer V-axis cosine is only 0.291.
missing.locator: Appendix S3, V-shape across architectures; Appendix S7

missing.what: Cross-lingual V-axis cosines are moderate (en–es 0.47, en–fr 0.16, es–fr 0.46).

record.verdict_notes: Several reader links were reassigned. Rows measuring alignment to human behavioural ratings or EEG (R5–R9) do not measure model-to-model similarity, so they were unlinked. R10 and R11 were moved from V3 to V1: they compare models of different architectures with an LLM direction against capability, not seeds. V6 rows concern LLM-to-brain alignment, so their bearing on model-to-model convergence is indirect. All cross-model comparisons concern one extracted 1-D direction. For models with different hidden sizes, the paper's 'cosine r' is probably a correlation of per-stimulus projections. The class-PC1 values in S12 (0.60–0.77) and S13 (about 0.43 at d=6) conflict. Preprint; no code released.

versions.untested_parts: No controlled sweep jointly varies model size, capability, architecture, objective, and training data; the main model-pair comparison concerns one extracted V-axis, not general representational distances over varied inputs.
The paper does not test whether vision and language model representations of paired images and captions become more aligned as both models improve.
The comparison concerns encoding of a V-axis or its subspaces, not recurrence of many features, individual units, or bases.
No general representation mapping, stitching, relative-representation transfer, or unpaired mapping is evaluated.
The V-axis is a low-dimensional extracted direction; the paper does not test recurrence of interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits.
The paper compares selected estimators and stimulus subsets, but does not systematically sweep similarity settings such as neighbour counts or broad out-of-distribution inputs.
The paper reports incomplete and non-uniform alignment, but does not experimentally distinguish shared training data or objectives from a common model of reality as its cause.

rows.subject: 36 EEG-emotion checkpoints from CBraMod and EMOD families
rows.stage_stated: trained on emotion labels; checkpoint variants include six recipe variants
rows.operation_detail: Association between class-mean V-axis encoding strength and balanced accuracy
rows.measure: Pearson correlation of class-mean V-axis encoding strength with BACC
rows.note: The checkpoints were trained on the nine emotion labels without V-axis loss; the paper reports that well-trained checkpoints recover the axis.
rows.check: This is the study's main capability-to-alignment result: better EEG classifiers align more with the LLM-derived direction (r = +0.885). It spans two architectures and six recipes, so it is not a seed-only comparison and does not bear on V3. Its specificity is limited by R13.

rows.measure: Pearson correlation of residual V-axis encoding with BACC
rows.note: The residual relation is described as statistically robust; residual encoding is also described as seed-specific.
rows.check: Within-class residual alignment with the LLM V-axis correlates with accuracy (r = +0.738). This is the authors' statistically robust signal. It does not measure seed-to-seed sharing, so V3 is removed.

rows.subject: 10 EMOD d=6 SOTA-pool checkpoints

labels.reason: R13 changes the null hypothesis used to assess specificity; the observed correlation remains 0.885. It does not show measured convergence weakening under another similarity measure or input choice.

labels.label: supports
labels.reason: R2 supports incomplete cross-family alignment relative to R1. This supports the incompleteness component, while family association alone does not establish a causal training-data explanation.

labels.label: challenges
labels.reason: R3 and R4 report near-complete agreement for the selected valence direction, with R4 explicitly conditional on Procrustes alignment.

relation.reason: Its own measurements bear on capability-associated alignment, shared structure across seeds, and incomplete cross-family agreement.

tranche.reason: The study reports its own cross-model results in a new, narrow valence-direction and EEG-classifier setting; its central question concerns supervision saturation.

source_check.notes: Statements accurately describe this study's restricted observables; their factual accuracy does not make every associated verdict valid. Figure 2 claims specificity despite p=0.066; Section 4 and Appendix S12 correctly state that this control is nonsignificant.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: V-axis similarity is already high but the reported size–alignment association is flat/non-significant, rather than increasing with size (R1, R5).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Across LLM families and model tiers
reader_labels.reason: Cross-family similarity is lower and more variable than within-Qwen3 similarity, and reported valence alignment ranges from a high-alignment tier to models below r = 0.4 (R2, R7, R8, R9).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: FACED EEG classifiers’ class-mean V-axis encoding
reader_labels.reason: Checkpoints trained without V-axis supervision encode the axis, and the 10-checkpoint pool has class-PC1 |r| in [0.60, 0.77] (R10, R12).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Residual V-axis encoding relates to accuracy but is described as seed-specific, so convergence is not complete across the full representation (R11).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: FACED stimulus subsets and selected similarity estimators
reader_labels.reason: The PO3/γ association is strong for the 9 emotional-pole stimuli and absent for the remaining 19; the mutual-information and linear analyses also differ in significance (R18, R19, R20, R21, R22).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Across model families and EEG checkpoint subspaces
reader_labels.reason: Alignment is not uniform across model families, and the shared class-mean direction coexists with seed-specific residual encoding (R2, R8, R9, R11).
